classification.difficultyReason: Use the explicit parallel-construction hint to split zigzag angles and combine transferred sectors, including reflex turns.

content.prompt: Find these angles (hint: construct a parallel line)

spec.description: Horizontal parallel lines through A and C, left-opening V at B, open rightward parallel chevrons, 28° at A and 37° at C.
spec.mathematics: AB descends at 28 degrees to the horizontal; CB rises at 37 degrees. The target angle is not marked or supplied.

answer.worked:
Construct a horizontal line through $B$, parallel to the marked lines. Alternate angles give $28^\circ$ and $37^\circ$ beside this line at $B$.
$$\begin{align*}\angle ABC&=28^\circ+37^\circ\\\angle ABC&=65^\circ.\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Horizontal parallel lines through A and C, right-opening V at B, D on the lower leftward ray; 47° at A and 112° at B.
spec.mathematics: BA has direction 47 degrees; BC has direction -65 degrees, giving 112 degrees at B.
spec.answerVisibility: No target angle value at C.

answer.worked:
Construct a horizontal line through $B$, parallel to the marked lines. Alternate angles give $47^\circ$ between $BA$ and the rightward constructed ray. Let the remaining angle at $B$ be $x^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}x+47&=112\\x&=65.\end{align*}$$
Thus $\angle BCD=65^\circ$ (alternate angles on parallel lines).

spec.description: Four-segment zigzag with matching upper-right parallel arrows on its first and last segments; 50° at the top, a° at the central vertex and 60° at the right vertex. No angle arcs.
spec.mathematics: Outer segments have direction 30 degrees. Central rays have directions 80 and -30 degrees, giving the source target sector.

answer.worked:
Construct a line through the vertex labelled $a^\circ$, parallel to the marked segments. Alternate angles split the target sector into $50^\circ$ and $60^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}a&=50+60\\a&=110.\end{align*}$$
Therefore $a=110^\circ$.

spec.description: Low 50° corner connected to a reflex-labelled target and a 120° intersection on an extended sloping parallel line. Matching arrows point upper-left.
spec.mathematics: Marked lines have direction 130 degrees. The low-to-target ray has direction 80 degrees and the target-to-right ray direction 10 degrees. The reflex target is selected explicitly.

answer.worked:
Construct a parallel to the marked lines through the target vertex. Co-interior angles give the angle beside the short connecting segment:
$$\begin{align*}x+120&=180\\x&=60.\end{align*}$$
Alternate angles give $50^\circ$ beside the other segment. Angles at a point give:
$$\begin{align*}a+50+60&=360\\a+110&=360\\a&=250.\end{align*}$$
Therefore $a=250^\circ$.

spec.description: Five-segment chain with vertical-to-horizontal right-angle corner, 50° at the upper vertex, 80° below the horizontal corner and a° at the low vertex. Outer diagonal arrows point upper-right.
spec.mathematics: Outer diagonals have direction 40 degrees. The low-to-80-degree-corner ray has direction 80 degrees. Right-angle marker is derived from the incident vertical and horizontal rays.

answer.worked:
Construct horizontal parallels through the upper vertex and the low vertex. The first marked diagonal makes $x^\circ$ with a horizontal:
$$\begin{align*}x+50&=90\\x&=40.\end{align*}$$
Parallel-line relationships give $40^\circ$ between the final marked diagonal and the rightward horizontal at the low vertex. Alternate angles give $80^\circ$ between that horizontal and the ray returning to the $80^\circ$ corner.
$$\begin{align*}a+40&=80\\a&=40.\end{align*}$$
Therefore $a=40^\circ$.

spec.description: Open chain with a° at the left horizontal corner, exterior 260° arc at the right horizontal corner, 30° at the peak and matching downward-right arrows on outer segments.
spec.mathematics: Left upward ray has direction 110 degrees; rising ray from the reflex corner has direction 80 degrees. The exterior arc spans 260 degrees.

answer.worked:
The smaller angle at the reflex-marked corner is $x^\circ$:
$$\begin{align*}x+260&=360\\x&=100.\end{align*}$$
Construct a line through this corner parallel to the marked outer segments. Alternate angles give $30^\circ$ beside the rising segment. The remaining angle is $y^\circ$:
$$\begin{align*}y+30&=100\\y&=70.\end{align*}$$
Co-interior angles give:
$$\begin{align*}a+70&=180\\a&=110.\end{align*}$$
Therefore $a=110^\circ$.

spec.description: Two vertical outer segments with upward parallel arrows joined by a peak-valley chain. Labels: 20° at left low vertex, a° inside peak, 280° below valley without an added arc, and 300° beside an exterior arc at upper-right.
spec.mathematics: First rising diagonal has direction 70 degrees; peak-to-valley direction is -70 degrees; valley-to-right direction is 30 degrees. Exterior selections are preserved.

answer.worked:
Angles at a point give the smaller angles at the valley and upper-right vertex:
$$\begin{align*}x+280&=360\\x&=80\\y+300&=360\\y&=60.\end{align*}$$
Construct vertical parallels through the valley and peak. Alternate angles give $60^\circ$ between the valley's right arm and its upward vertical. Let the angle on the other side of this vertical be $z^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}z+60&=80\\z&=20.\end{align*}$$
Parallel-line relationships give two $20^\circ$ angles beside the downward vertical at the peak.
$$\begin{align*}a&=20+20\\a&=40.\end{align*}$$
Therefore $a=40^\circ$.

spec.description: Vertical parallel outer segments with upward arrows, rising shoulder-to-peak segment, descending peak-to-notch segment and rising notch-to-right segment. Labels 140° and 70° at shoulders, reflex a° at peak; right-angle square at notch.
spec.mathematics: Shoulder-to-peak direction 50 degrees, peak-to-notch direction -70 degrees, notch-to-right direction 20 degrees. The notch angle is 90 degrees and the peak target is reflex.

answer.worked:
Construct vertical parallels through the peak and the right-angle notch. Co-interior angles give the angle between the peak's left arm and the downward vertical:
$$\begin{align*}x+140&=180\\x&=40.\end{align*}$$
Alternate angles transfer $70^\circ$ to the notch. Its right angle gives:
$$\begin{align*}y+70&=90\\y&=20.\end{align*}$$
Alternate angles transfer $20^\circ$ to the other side of the downward vertical at the peak. Angles at a point give:
$$\begin{align*}a+40+20&=360\\a+60&=360\\a&=300.\end{align*}$$
Therefore $a=300^\circ$.
